analysis:
Integration pass over the stop-string scoping change. The PR adds ReasoningStopScope.swift, threads an optional per-request stopStringScope through MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine, EngineV2Bridge+Submission (submitTokenized and cbv2Request, lines ~63/83/136/325-329/1073), EngineV2Bridge+Events (runPump/pump) and EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence (matchedStopSequence with scope). It also adds docs, a changelog entry, tests and a libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule bump. The replayed source confirms the effect is limited to where client stop strings match in generated text: reasoning and tool-call spans are excluded for qwen3, deepseekR1 and gemma4, and the native block engine gets nil. Matched-stop attribution now requires a candidate that alone reproduces the same StopHoldback scan.

No change to encryption, attestation, authorization, coordinator-provider framing, cacheScope/cacheSalt, SSD prefix cache (T-041, SEC-035 unchanged) or the reservation, staging and retirement release paths. The scope is chosen in-process from the parser format and the prompt probe. It is not derived from a consumer-supplied cache or auth value. A client controls only its own stop strings, so the worst case is truncation of its own output. The reasoning-prefix probe move in the media path keeps the existing do/catch release handling. The removal of the two post-submit checkFirstContentDeadline calls is a minor latency/availability matter, since makeDeadlineCheckedEventStream still enforces deadlines. It is not a security regression.

Unverified: the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule bump (7933a0f to 7f00abc) is not reviewable from the supplied evidence, and it implements CBv2StopStringScope and StopHoldback, so it affects the TB-007 inference engine. Integration replay is incomplete (80 omitted units). Requesting deeper review of the submodule diff and of the unseen portions of the scheduler patch.
